headline: Bank Indonesia Raises Benchmark Interest Rate To Six Percent Level
seoTitle: Bank Indonesia Increases Benchmark Interest Rate to 6…
metaDescription: Bank Indonesia has officially raised its benchmark interest rate to 6 percent, citing global economic uncertainty and the need to stabilize the rupiah.
aiSummaryBullets: Bank Indonesia increased its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 6 percent during its November 2026 meeting.
The policy adjustment also impacts the central bank's Deposit Facility and Lending Facility rates.
Officials stated the decision aims to bolster rupiah stability and mitigate risks from persistent global economic volatility.
aiContextParagraph: During its Board of Governors meeting held on November 17-18, 2026, Bank Indonesia (BI) officially implemented a 25 basis point hike to the national benchmark interest rate, bringing the BI Rate to 6 percent. This move marks the sixth time the central bank has raised interest rates throughout 2026. According to the institution, the decision was necessitated by ongoing uncertainty in the global economy, which has contributed to increased volatility in financial markets. By adjusting the rate, the central bank aims to strengthen the value of the Indonesian rupiah and maintain domestic economic stability. The policy shift extends to associated financial instruments, specifically the Deposit Facility and the Lending Facility, which also saw corresponding increases. This action underscores the central bank's proactive stance in managing current macroeconomic pressures and addressing the impact of international financial fluctuations on the local market.
